variants: Blue Mountains National Park covers about 2,680 km2 of sandstone plateau, cut by deep valleys, on Sydney's western edge, and is the most central of the eight protected areas in the World Heritage-listed Greater Blue Mountains Area. Most visitors base themselves in Katoomba, about 103 km west of Sydney, where Echo Point looks across the Jamison Valley to the Three Sisters rock formation and Scenic World runs railway and cable rides into the rainforest below the cliffs. More than 140 km of tracks lead along the rim and down to waterfalls, with Leura, Wentworth Falls, Blackheath and Mount Victoria all a short drive or train ride away. Some tracks are closed for long periods, so check the NPWS alerts before choosing a walk.

Set 103 km west of Sydney, this national park is a plateau of sandstone cliffs and forested valleys, part of the Greater Blue Mountains Area that UNESCO inscribed in 2000. The Three Sisters at Echo Point in Katoomba are the best-known sight, and the nearby towns of Leura, Wentworth Falls, Blackheath and Mount Victoria give access to waterfalls, the Grose Valley lookouts and over 140 km of walking tracks. Visitors arrive by road or by train from Sydney Central, which takes about two hours. Track closures after landslides and storms are common, so the NPWS alerts page is worth reading first.

The Blue Mountains are a World Heritage-listed stretch of sandstone cliffs, canyons and waterfalls managed as a 2,680 km2 national park by NSW National Parks and Wildlife Service. Katoomba is the usual base, with the Three Sisters and Echo Point, Scenic World's railway and skyway, and a cliff-top track network that links Wentworth Falls, Leura and Katoomba. Blackheath, about 15 minutes' drive north, looks over the Grose Valley, a declared wilderness area. The district is a day trip from Sydney, though the train takes about two hours each way.

Tracks close often and some for long periods, including part of National Pass after a landslide and the Govetts descent at Blackheath; check the NPWS alerts page before you set out.

Trains from Sydney Central run to Katoomba and Leura without reservations and take about two hours; local bus 686 links Katoomba station, Echo Point and Scenic World, but Wentworth Falls, Leura Cascades and Govetts Leap need a bus, taxi or car.
The mountains can be up to 10 C colder than the coast and fog can hide the views all day in cold, wet weather; set your GPS to 'Echo Point, Katoomba', since 'Blue Mountains' routes to unsealed roads.
Several walks are shut with no reopening date, among them parts of National Pass and Lower Fern Bower; the NPWS alerts page is the current list.

Without a car, take the train to Katoomba (about two hours from Sydney Central, no seat booking) and the 686 bus to Echo Point and Scenic World; check the timetable and Opal fares on transport.nsw.gov.au.

Parking at Echo Point is paid (Wikivoyage gives about $8 an hour); parking free at Scenic World and walking is the suggested alternative. Fog is common over the valley in winter, so check the forecast and search 'Echo Point, Katoomba' on GPS.
